description: Cross-binding conformance for esm-spec 6.6.5's inline `reference` scope: 'an inline Expression whose free variables are the domain dimension names'. For a field shaped over index sets the dimension names are the asserted variable's `shape` entries, each bound at every grid point to the 1-based position along its axis (the index space `coords` reads, convention 1). Before this category all three executing bindings evaluated the reference as ONE build-time array expression and sampled it per cell, so a dimension name mentioned free was simply unbound (Rust E_TREEWALK_UNBOUND_NAME, Python 'Unresolved symbol', Julia UNBOUND_VARIABLE) and authors had to spell every reference as an explicit `aggregate(i from x; ...)` gather. The fixture asserts one exact decay field through the free-name analytic form, a table lookup by the dimension name, the explicit gather, and a gather that rebinds the dimension name as its own loop symbol (which must NOT be wrapped a second time), plus a reference-free `mean` as the regression guard; all must agree on the golden actuals. Julia is the reference binding and minted golden/reference_dimension_names.json through its own `run_pde_tests`. The right-hand side is linear decay of a per-cell constant field, so every pinned solver family reproduces exp(-t) to the assertion tolerances.

scope_excluded.go: rewrite-only port; no makearray lowering / simulator / inline PDE-test runner
scope_excluded.typescript: rewrite-only port; no makearray lowering / simulator / inline PDE-test runner

tolerances.note: assertion_atol is 1e-9 rather than the 1e-11 of the sibling pde_inline_* categories because assertion 2's actual (the L2 error of u(t=1) against the analytic reference) IS the time-integrator's residual: Julia Tsit5 leaves 1.8e-14, Python RK45 5.2e-11 at the pinned rtol=1e-12/atol=1e-14. Every other actual is either exactly 0 (t=0 forms) or O(1) (the table Linf_error) and is gated by assertion_rtol.

assertions.reference_form: table lookup indexed by the dimension name
gather rebinding the dimension name as its loop symbol
